title: Triage a failed VCF Automation 9.1 deployment from PowerShell
prompt:
Our payments platform runs on VCF Automation in VMware Cloud Foundation 9.1 (the service that replaced vRealize Automation and Aria Automation). A UAT deployment is sitting in a failed state after a day-2 action ran overnight. The on-call runbook for this currently says "log into the UI and click through the request history", which nobody does reliably at 3am and which we cannot script.

This repository holds `VcfAutomation.Triage`, a PowerShell module whose functions are all stubs that throw. Implement them so on-call can diagnose and remediate a failed deployment from a terminal.

Start with `docs/contract.json`. It is the REST contract for the VCF Automation deployment operations you may call. VCF Automation publishes no API specification, so the contract was transcribed by hand from Broadcom's reference documentation; each operation records the `docUrl` it came from, and `docs/official_sources.json` lists every page. Do not call an operation the contract does not name.

What to build, in `src/VcfAutomation.Triage/VcfAutomation.Triage.psm1`:

1. The six operation wrappers that are already stubbed there, one per contract operation.

2. `Invoke-VcfAutomationDeploymentTriage -BaseUri <uri> -AccessToken <token> -DeploymentName <name>`. It has to pull the evidence rather than assume it:
   - resolve the deployment by name, filtering server-side rather than listing the whole org and sifting locally;
   - find the request on that deployment whose status is `FAILED`. This is not necessarily the newest request on the deployment;
   - enumerate that request's events and find the one that carries logs;
   - read that event's log rows and lift out of them (a) the vCenter correlation id, which the logs record in the form `correlationId=<value>`, and (b) the log message that reports the failed vCenter task;
   - submit the remediation: re-run the same action that failed. That action takes no inputs. The reason you send must cite both the id of the failed request and the correlation id you found in the log;
   - read the submitted request back.

   Return one object carrying these properties: `DeploymentId`, `DeploymentName`, `DeploymentStatus`, `FailedRequestId`, `FailedActionId`, `FailureEventId`, `FailureEventResourceName`, `CorrelationId`, `RootCauseMessage`, `RemediationRequestId`, `RemediationRequestStatus`.

3. Wire discipline. The contract's `wireRules` are load-bearing: an optional query parameter or request-body field that the caller did not supply must be absent from the wire, not present and empty. PowerShell makes this easy to get wrong, since `ConvertTo-Json` over a hashtable holding `$null`, `''` or `@{}` will emit them happily. Every request must also carry the required headers the contract lists.

VCF PowerCLI (the `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.*` modules) is installed on this machine as a prerequisite of the wider toolchain and is already declared in the module manifest under `ExternalModuleDependencies`. Do not vendor it into the repository and do not move it into `RequiredModules`.

`mock/vcfa_mock.py` is a loopback stand-in for a VCF Automation appliance, pinned to the contract. Run it by hand while you work, as `README.md` describes: it refuses requests that violate the contract and records every request it receives, which makes it a fast way to check your request shapes.

Check your work with `python3 tests/verify.py`. Treat `docs/`, `mock/` and `tests/` as read-only.

prerequisites.name: PowerShell
prerequisites.reason: The deliverable is a PowerShell module and the test driver is a .ps1 script.

prerequisites.name: Python
prerequisites.reason: Runs the loopback mock and the verification suite. Standard library only.

prerequisites.name: VCF.PowerCLI
prerequisites.reason: VCF PowerCLI supplies the VMware.Sdk.Vcf.* modules that the wider operator toolchain is built on. The seed never vendors them; the module manifest declares them under PrivateData.PSData.ExternalModuleDependencies so that importing the module does not hard-fail if the SDK is absent. Note that the VMware.Sdk.Vcf family covers CloudBuilder, SddcManager, Installer and Ops only - VCF Automation has no generated binding because it has no published specification, which is why the module's VCF Automation calls are hand-rolled REST against docs/contract.json.

verification.description: Starts contract-pinned loopback mocks on free 127.0.0.1 ports, runs the triage orchestrator and a direct probe of all six operation wrappers, then asserts the returned artifacts and exact wire shape of every recorded request - including omission of unset optional fields and preservation of supplied optional values.
